page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The rule
lines: Huckel's rule: a compound is aromatic
if its ring is planar, cyclic and
where n is a whole number,
steps.why: The rule is a count with conditions attached, so all four parts belong in the statement: the ring must be flat, closed and conjugated before the electron count is applied at all. A flat conjugated ring holding 4n π electrons instead of 4n + 2 is not aromatic.
common_mistakes: Writing 4n + 2 without saying π electrons. Only the π electrons are counted.
Leaving out planar, cyclic and conjugated. The electron count on its own is not the whole rule.
steps.memory_tip: Flat, closed, conjugated, and 4n + 2 π electrons.
steps.margin_note: Write the three conditions and the formula on the page, not the formula alone.

steps.label: The example
lines: Benzene C₆H₆ has a planar, cyclic and
It is drawn with three C=C bonds, so
steps.why: Benzene is the standard test of the rule: the ring is drawn with three double bonds, which gives six π electrons, and six is exactly what the formula returns for n = 1, so benzene satisfies the rule and is aromatic.
common_mistakes: Counting every electron in the ring. Only the π electrons are counted — those of the double bonds, and a lone pair that is delocalised into the ring. Benzene has 6.
Writing n = 6 for benzene. The count of π electrons is 6, and the value of n is 1.
steps.memory_tip: Benzene is drawn with three double bonds, so six π electrons, and n = 1.
steps.margin_note: Show the substitution 4(1) + 2 = 6 in figures, not only in words.

insider_note: The rule is often written as the formula alone. The words planar, cyclic and conjugated are part of it, and one worked example with the value of n makes the short answer complete.
